verdict.rationale: Lium is a GPU rental marketplace, so offering managed Slurm or Kubernetes is a fair question for it. The pack never mentions Slurm, Kubernetes or any managed job scheduler. The closest items, RDMA clusters of whole machines and per-pod job execution via the CLI and SDK, are raw-node rental and one-off execution, not a managed scheduling layer. They are adjacent capabilities and earn no credit.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can schedule jobs on managed Slurm or Kubernetes instead of building my own scheduler on raw nodes
